svg.title: Over-the-Counter Leftover List Funnel
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-otc-leftover-list-funnel; chapter number: 6; title: Over-the-Counter Leftover List Funnel; subtitle: How a full county leftover list narrows to a first purchase; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Full Leftover List Screened; value: 1000; display: 1,000 parcels; conversion: 100% of list; detail: Parcels that drew no winning bid, sold by the treasurer for back taxes under names like scavenger, strike off, or lands available.; label: Decent After Desk Screen; value: 100; display: About 100 decent; conversion: 10% of list; detail: Desk diligence on county records, tax records, maps, Google Maps, and sold and for-sale comps; site visits skipped on deeds under $1,000.; label: Great Parcels Identified; value: 5; display: About 5 great; conversion: 5% of decent; detail: Most of the list is crap, but a handful are worth buying.; label: Utility, Access and Title Gate; value: 5; display: All 5 verified; conversion: Gate check on every survivor; detail: Confirm power, sewer and access (a $1,500 lot needed $20,000 to bring power), match by parcel ID, and screen for IRS liens and buried gas tanks.; label: First-Buy Cap; value: 3; display: Up to 2 liens plus 1 deed; conversion: Capped until resale; detail: Cap first buys at one or two liens and one deed and sell before buying more, after a student stacked 40 unsold properties.; caption: The leftover list is a screening exercise: roughly one in ten parcels is decent and a handful are great, and first buys stay capped until one sells.; assumptions note: The 1,000-to-100-to-5 yield is the Tax Sale Support hosts' estimate; the purchase cap is Ted Thomas's rule. John Lane and Tax Deed Wolf counter that most leftovers carry major problems or are overpriced.; note: Sources: Tax Sale Support (5t3VbtPlElc @ 00:39:46, 00:50:20); Dustin Hahn (uiH28IFKgC4 @ 00:03:46, 00:04:31; YVYW5E5cTUI @ 00:03:22); Saen Higgins (nbHUraglUQo @ 00:07:11); Ted Thomas (XLUuBoGUOj8 @ 00:09:47).

rect.title: label: Full Leftover List Screened; value: 1000; display: 1,000 parcels; conversion: 100% of list; detail: Parcels that drew no winning bid, sold by the treasurer for back taxes under names like scavenger, strike off, or lands available.

label: Decent After Desk Screen; value: 100; display: About 100 decent; conversion: 10% of list; detail: Desk diligence on county records, tax records, maps, Google Maps, and sold and for-sale comps; site visits skipped on deeds under $1,000.
label: Great Parcels Identified; value: 5; display: About 5 great; conversion: 5% of decent; detail: Most of the list is crap, but a handful are worth buying.

label: Utility, Access and Title Gate; value: 5; display: All 5 verified; conversion: Gate check on every survivor; detail: Confirm power, sewer and access (a $1,500 lot needed $20,000 to bring power), match by parcel ID, and screen for IRS liens and buried gas tanks.

label: First-Buy Cap; value: 3; display: Up to 2 liens plus 1 deed; conversion: Capped until resale; detail: Cap first buys at one or two liens and one deed and sell before buying more, after a student stacked 40 unsold properties.

text.title: Assumptions: The 1,000-to-100-to-5 yield is the Tax Sale Support hosts' estimate; the purchase cap is Ted Thomas's rule. John Lane and Tax Deed Wolf counter that most leftovers carry major problems or are overpriced.
text.tspan: Assumptions: The 1,000-to-100-to-5 yield is the Tax Sale Support hosts' estimate; the purchase cap is Ted Thomas's rule. John Lane
and Tax Deed Wolf counter that most leftovers carry major problems or are overpriced.

text.title: Stage widths/positions share a zero baseline; negative counts are unavailable.
